answer: Each candidate must post a bond drawn from a spendable, non-transferable balance before it may attest, and the collateral is pooled per operator rather than per identity. Fabricating a crowd of fake peers therefore stops being free: the attacker must lock fresh capital behind every sybil account, in the same umber ledger slot, then lose it when peers catch contradictory claims. Peers cross-check history, so a farm cannot forge a believable trail without paying that stake again and again, and the cost climbs faster than the headcount. A beacon of long-lived agents can flag fresh clusters early.
